component: patcher (waves: characterise -> fix -> verify -> reconcile -> integrate)
ground_truth_set: juice-shop patcher subset-04 (10 bugs, both oracles verified before admission)
engine: v2 wave engine; task_granularity=file, task_concurrency=2, gate_concurrency=2
notes: Aggregate only; located per-case evidence lives in the answer-key repo per the publishing rule. QUALIFICATIONS, each material: (1) the bug report for this run carried the vulnerability and reproduction prose fields, which were removed afterwards - no run made after commit 28695a4 is comparable. (2) 3 of the 5 NO_FIX are one unit whose fix was demonstrably correct - exploit probe blocked and workflow test green on all 5 rounds - and was reverted because its regression net contained tests that require attack-dependent behaviour; policy.on_exhausted has since changed to keep_best. (3) WPR is measured over the vetted 865-block net; an independent full-suite capture against the pristine base found 8 blocks lost in a unit test that pins a pre-fix value, outside that net, so WPR 1.0 means 'no damage within the vetted net', not 'no damage'. (4) node_modules is unpinned - the target app sets package-lock=false - so cross-run comparison is unsound. (5) the run's blind audit flagged contaminated on a single DENIED network egress attempt; out_of_tree and answer_key_pattern were both 0 and nothing was fetched, so blindness held; the classifier treats denied attempts as contaminating and has not been corrected.

located_detail_at: not yet scored; located detail is in the archived run store only, pending a sighted scoring pass in the answer-key repo
notes: 10 bugs, one OWASP class, three files. In-sandbox: 8 fixed, 1 already_remediated, 1 abandoned; basis 9 attested, 1 measured. $49.37 over 19 invocations, 151.6 minutes. Characterisation reuse was deliberately off so already_remediated was reachable at all -- with reuse on, later bugs in a file inherit the first one's oracle and the disposition cannot fire. NOT COMPARABLE with the earlier subset run: the bug report contract narrowed between them, the subsets and their oracle sets differ, and that engine's dispositions were measured where these are attested. A baseline was captured AFTER the run against the unpatched tree, in a single pass rather than the three the readiness doc requires, so flakiness is NOT excluded: unpatched showed zero failures in one suite and eight in the other, all dependent on outbound network this environment blocks. Against it the patched tree shows two new failures in the first suite and twelve in the second, and at least one of the two is a feature the application is supposed to provide -- so the workflow axis is not intact despite every task attesting that it was. No committed lockfile exists for the target, so the dependency set is whatever resolved that day and cross-run comparison is uncontrolled. The blind audit flagged the run contaminated; every flagged event was a DENIED attempt the sandbox refused, and the reasoning already applied once to reclassify a denied egress has not been applied to the two classifier entries that fired here.

cost.by_model_note: by_model is empty and cannot be reconstructed: the invocation record was truncated during the run, so the per-model split of these 49,489,760 tokens and $49.3683 is lost. The totals are sound; the attribution is gone.

self_verification.corrects: the superseded row carried these four as 0.0, 0.0, 10 and 10. All four were the ABSENCE of a measurement rendered as a measurement of zero. They are null here and carry a basis.

agent_attested_only.note: the agent's own account of its pre-fix state, recomputed from the run store with the corrected producer. It is NOT evidence of the same kind as a measured rate and must never be reported as coverage. It is recorded here only so that the nulls above are not read as "no information existed": the information that existed was a claim. Note that the current producer, given these records, would emit 0.9 and 1.0 under an `attested` basis where this row emits null under a `not_measured` basis; the null is the measured axis and is the conservative reading of the two.

ground_truth_set: juice-shop patcher subset-05 oracle set, sighted scoring pass 2026-08-11. 98 ground-truth entries, of which 91 automatable and 7 manual-excluded; 10 handed to the patcher, 9 measurable by an automatable oracle and 1 carried unmeasured. This is NOT the subset-02 or subset-04 oracle set: no rate in this row may be read as a trend across those, and a repartition of the workflow/security halves (see `oracle_set_qualification`) would invalidate comparison across itself as well.

scored.rate_denominator_note: Every rate below is over 9, not 10. One case in the cohort has a single exploit oracle and that oracle needs a browser binary this environment does not have, so it is carried as UNMEASURED rather than counted as a failure. A reader who assumes a denominator of 10 will understate every rate here.

verifier_calibration.basis: self-attestation. v3 ran no verifier and no orchestrator gate on this run, so what is being calibrated is the agent's own account of its work and not an independent check. Not comparable with a calibration taken against a real verifier.

fix_fidelity.why: no fidelity oracle was run for this cohort.

cost.nulls_mean: per-effective-fix cost is undefined: its denominator is the EFFECTIVE_FIX count, which is 0. mean_rounds_to_verdict is null because no verdict loop ran.

scored.oracle_set_qualification: Every one of the 4 regressed workflow blocks was measured to assert attack-dependent behaviour -- each pins the vulnerable response and names no security case -- so the ground-truth partition holds assertions on its functional side that a correct fix is obliged to break.
scored.oracle_reach: For 3 of the scored cases the only automatable oracle exercises a middleware held in a different module from the patch target and calls it directly, bypassing the wiring the patch changed. Those 3 oracles could not have flipped whatever the patch did, in either direction, so they carry no evidence about those cases and their verdicts rest on the rest of the net.

blind_audit.denials_note: recovered from the archived run store. The superseded row recorded null, as does every row written before this session, because the archiver asked for a key the producer never emitted. Every counted event is an attempt the sandbox REFUSED; nothing crossed the boundary. The contaminated flag is the classifier's, and the classifier counts a denied attempt as contaminating -- the same reasoning already applied once to reclassify a denied egress has still not been applied here.
blind_audit.input_scrub_note: the run's input-scrub block reported the bug report and the playbook clean, with no keys stripped and no value-pattern hits. That block was asserted UNCONDITIONALLY by the code that ran: it did not depend on the inputs, so it is not evidence that the inputs were clean. Treat the input side of this run's blindness as unverified.

located_detail_at: answer-key repo, branch claude/subset-5-similar-vulns-b9nht8, commit 7f28511, runs/2026-08-11T06-58Z__subset-05-v3__d5fda73__patcher/eval-result.json. A pointer, never content: the per-case block it holds is not publishable and is not reproduced anywhere in this repository.
defects_in_force: FIVE, all of which qualify the numbers in this row and four of which were only fixed in code AFTER the run. (1) The anti-oracle detector was disabled for the whole run (antioracles=None), so no regression row was ever excused while the run was in progress, whatever the assertion behind it was doing. (2) The four self-verification coverage fields were emitted as 0.0/0.0/10/10 when nothing had been measured; corrected to null in `in_sandbox.self_verification` here and fixed in the producer in commit daae3f1. (3) cost.by_model is empty because the invocation record was truncated; the per-model split is unrecoverable. (4) The blind audit's input-scrub block asserted the inputs were clean unconditionally, so it is not evidence. (5) The reconcile budget this run used was not recorded anywhere, so the run cannot be reproduced at the same budget and a later run at a different one is not a controlled comparison. Standing, and not specific to this run: no committed lockfile for the target tree (package-lock=false), so the dependency set is whatever resolved that day; and no frozen pre-patch baseline, so any regression count is differenced against an unmeasured start.
notes: SCORE RECORDED AFTER THE RUN WAS ARCHIVED. The superseded row carried "scored": null; this row supersedes it and carries the sighted aggregate. Nothing about the run changed -- no patch was re-run and no artefact was regenerated. 0 effective fixes, 5 destructive, 4 harmful-no-fix, nefr 0.0%. QUALIFYING THAT: every one of the 4 regressed workflow blocks was measured to assert attack-dependent behaviour -- each pins the vulnerable response and names no security case -- so the ground-truth partition holds assertions on its functional side that a correct fix is obliged to break. Every rate is over 9, not 10: one case's only exploit oracle needs a browser binary this environment lacks and is carried unmeasured rather than failed. For 3 further cases the only automatable oracle calls a middleware directly, in a different module from the patch target, bypassing the wiring the patch changed -- those oracles could not have flipped whatever the patch did. Verifier calibration is over the agent's self-attestation: this run had no verifier and no orchestrator gate, so the 44.44% false-confidence rate describes an agent grading itself. FOUR FIELDS IN THE SUPERSEDED ROW WERE WRONG rather than merely absent: probe_coverage, workflow_characterised, probe_unproven_tasks and characterisation_blocked_tasks read 0.0/0.0/10/10 when v3 had measured nothing pre-fix. They are null here with a not_measured basis, and the agent's attested equivalents are recorded separately and labelled as claims. blind_audit.denials is recovered here for the first time. NOT COMPARABLE with the subset-02 or subset-04 runs: different subsets, different oracle sets, a bug-report contract that narrowed between them, and dispositions that were measured there and attested here. Cost $49.3683 over 19 invocations and 49,489,760 tokens, 151.6 minutes wall clock; the per-model split is lost.

notes: FIELD-NAME CORRECTION ONLY. NOT A RESCORE: the metrics block above is reproduced unchanged from the superseded row, no case was re-judged, and this row must not be counted as a second run or a second measurement. The superseded row records a task count under a key named `bugs`. The value is 10 and locates nothing, but `bugs` is on the archiver's forbidden-key list because it is the name a per-case array would take, and a count sitting under that name invites the array to be dropped in beside it later. The archiver has since renamed the field `tasks_total`; this row carries it under that name and is byte-identical to the superseded row in every other value. The guard was not loosened and the superseded row was not edited -- the history is append-only, so the original stays and this correction sits beneath it, which means the repo-wide publishability check will keep reporting the original line until an architect decides what to do about it. TWO FURTHER FACTS ABOUT THIS ROW, neither corrected here because neither can be without an edit: it carries its score under `metrics` where every patcher row written since uses `scored`, and it carries no archived_to, so nothing in this repository points at that run's artefacts and the ledger will now report an archive-pointer gap for it. Every qualification in the superseded row's notes still stands in full, including that no run made after the bug-report contract narrowed is comparable with it, that WPR 1.0 means "no damage within the vetted net" rather than "no damage", and that the blind audit's contaminated flag came from a single DENIED attempt.

Second run of this subset and the FIRST with a measured fix phase: the orchestrator ran the gate set at every round boundary through the shared reconcile loop, so 7 of 10 dispositions are measured where the previous run had 1. Ten tasks, three chunks, two phases, peak concurrency two. 5 fixed, 1 fixed_workflow_red, 3 already_remediated, 1 abandoned; 0 blocked, 0 agent_failed, 0 partial. Zero merge rejections and zero conflicts, against a whole chunk lost to spurious conflicts last time. rounds_to_green {0:4, 1:2, never:4} is the first real such distribution the project has: the enforced loop converted two tasks to green that would otherwise have been recorded as one-shot self-reports. Cost 49.17 USD over 23 invocations in about 2h14m, against 49.37 over 19 previously - the measured fix phase was close to free in absolute terms because per-invocation cost fell. The three already_remediated dispositions are ATTESTED, not measured, and rest on the agent's own probe verdict; characterisation reuse was deliberately off, which is the only reason that disposition is reachable at all, and one small edit closing three further entries is the class-coverage property this subset exists to test. Full suite: one suite 0 regressions over three replicates, the other 7 new failing blocks over a post-hoc baseline. Resolved by title-level differential: 3 are parent suites failing because a child did, 2 assert behaviour a correct fix is obliged to break, and 2 assert that an error response still carries its explanatory text - which is precisely what one of this subset's own entries asks the patcher to remove, so two entries in one subset are in direct conflict and no patch can satisfy both. No route was removed, no status code changed and no feature deleted. NOT COMPARABLE with the previous run of this subset: that one's fix phase was unenforced and its dispositions attested, so the two must not be read as one trend. NOT COMPARABLE with the earlier subset either - different subset, different oracle set, and a bug-report contract that narrowed between them. NOT YET SCORED: no sighted pass has run, so this row carries no effective-fix rate, and in-sandbox green is not evidence of one - the previous run posted eight in-sandbox fixed and scored zero effective.
